memory_diag.read_by: harness check memory_diag_fresh; 98's progress page; readout 4 of memory_layers_0905

name.why: the ARM name (m1, m2, m3), not the run kind. Readout 3 is M2 vs M1 vs the control and 98 draws three curves, so a ledger keyed only on step folds the three arms into one line. --name from the launch, so it matches the experiments row and the checkpoint.

step.why: optimizer step, not tokens: the stop rules in readouts 4 and 5 are stated in steps (tok/s at 30, pool_touched at 1000) and a reader must not have to convert.

pool_touched_frac.why: fraction of memory values touched in the window since the last row -- readout 4's collapse detector, stop below 0.20 at step 1000. A FRACTION, not a count: the count is not comparable between M1 (1,048,576 values) and M2 (262,144), which is the comparison readout 3 exists to make.

topk_entropy.why: entropy of the top-k weight distribution in nats, mean over the window. 0 means one value takes all the weight; ln(k)=ln(32)=3.466 is uniform over the top-k. Unbounded above is wrong but harmless -- pinning max=ln(k) here would make the schema depend on the arm's k.

key_gini.why: Gini of the key-usage histogram over the window. 0 is uniform use, 1 is one key. Distinguishes the two collapse shapes pool_touched_frac cannot separate: a pool can be 90% touched and still be one hot key per row.

tok_s_gpu.why: readout 5's stop rule: below 70000 at step 30 the arm stops. Per GPU, so it compares against the control's 82K regardless of world size -- an aggregate would read as a pass at any world.

n_values.why: size of the pool this row measured. Optional and recorded anyway: pool_touched_frac is a ratio, and a ratio whose denominator is not written down cannot be re-derived if the arm's config is later disputed.

topk.why: the k of the top-k. Same reason as n_values: it is the scale of topk_entropy, and ln(k) is the only reference value a reader can compare against.

rows_changed_since_prev.why: readout 6, write effectiveness: rows of the value table whose fp32 checksum changed since the previous diag row, as a FRACTION OF TOUCHED ROWS. Stop below 0.50. It exists because the other four diagnostics cannot see a frozen table -- pool_touched_frac, topk_entropy and key_gini are all functions of the SELECTION distribution, which the keys produce, and the keys have an fp32 master; a table whose every bf16 update rounds to zero reads healthy on all three. NOT capped at 1.0: the denominator is this window's touched count, and a row touched in an earlier window can change in this one, so a ratio above 1 is a real observation rather than a bad number. ABSENT on a run's first diag row, where no previous checksum exists -- an absence means not measured, a 0.0 would mean nothing moved, and the two must not be spelled the same.

rows_changed.why: the raw count behind rows_changed_since_prev, kept beside the fraction because the fraction alone cannot say whether a small value came from a small numerator or a small denominator. Measured by projecting each row of the table onto one seeded random vector in fp32 (model._ROW_PROBE_SEED) -- 4 bytes per ROW rather than 2 bytes per parameter, so 4 MiB at M1 against 4 GiB for keeping a copy of the previous table.

ts.why: wall clock, UTC, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. The freshness check uses step distance, not time, because a stalled run keeps its last step while the clock advances -- so this is for humans reading the file, never for a gate.

moe_diag.written_by: train.py, every 100 steps, rank 0 only, via scripts/moe_diag.py log_diag
moe_diag.read_by: harness check moe_diag_fresh; readout 4 of moe_0905 (usage < 0.50 at step 300, normalised entropy < 0.70 at step 500)

name.why: the ARM name (e1, e1b), not the run kind. E1b is the layer-count axis against E1, so a ledger keyed only on step folds two arms into one curve; --mem_arm's analogue, from the launch line so it matches the experiments row and the checkpoint.

step.why: optimizer step, not tokens: readout 4's stop rules are stated in steps (usage at 300, entropy at 500) and a reader must not have to convert.

ts.why: UTC timestamp, and it is part of the ROW IDENTITY rather than decoration. A relaunched arm re-visits its own step numbers, so (name, step) is not unique across runs of one arm -- measured on the memory ledger, where it collided three ways on a relaunch. The ledger carries no run id, so ts is the only field separating two runs.

window_steps.why: how many steps the counters in this row cover. REQUIRED, not optional, because every other metric here is a per-window statistic and a fraction without its window length is not comparable to another row's: the memory ledger's windows were 1-10, 11-20, 21-30, 31-100 then every 100 (diagnostics(reset=True) clears the counters), and a trend read across those windows had to be withdrawn. 44's review of moe_0905 made this field a condition.

usage_frac.why: fraction of routed experts receiving at least one token in the window -- readout 4's collapse detector, STOP below 0.50 at step 300. A FRACTION, not a count, because E1 has 24 routed experts and E1b has 48 and readout 3 compares them.

entropy_norm.why: token-count entropy over experts divided by ln(N) -- STOP below 0.70 at step 500. Normalised so the bar is one number across expert counts; unnormalised entropy at 24 experts and at 48 are not on the same scale.

load_gini.why: Gini of the per-expert token counts. Carried alongside usage_frac because the two separate the collapse shapes: every expert can receive a token (usage 1.0) while one takes most of them, which is the regime the balancer is supposed to prevent and usage_frac alone cannot see.

tokens.why: routed token-slots counted in the window (tokens x top_k, summed over the window's steps). The denominator behind every fraction above, written so a reader can tell 'no forward ran' (0) from 'perfectly collapsed' -- both of which would otherwise print as usage_frac 0.0.

n_routed.why: routed experts in the arm, so a row is readable without joining to the launch line.

top_k.why: routed experts per token, same reason.

tok_s_gpu.why: throughput at this step. OPTIONAL here, unlike in memory_diag: readout 5's 0.85 bar is read at steps 30 and 100 only, because from step 200 on the memory arms shared the machine and a same-step comparison after 100 measures co-residency rather than the architecture (facts/memory_layers.json#mem.m1_throughput_cost). Written when known, omitted rather than defaulted when not.

novel_ops_4way.written_by: eval/novel_ops_4way.py:745, one row per checkpoint, appended INSIDE the scoring loop so an interrupt three arms in leaves those three on disk
novel_ops_4way.read_by: readout_1 of conversion_rate_0905 (runs/prereg.jsonl): arm minus control_arm accuracy, per program, never pooled

ckpt.why: basename of the scored checkpoint, e.g. ckpt_e1_conv_n64.pt. Part of the row identity. The BASENAME rather than the path, because the same checkpoint is scored from /work/aupai on the pod and would otherwise key differently than from a local clone.

readout.why: constant 'novel_ops_4way'. Present so a row read out of a merged or concatenated stream still names the instrument that produced it, rather than relying on the file it was found in.

items_sha256.why: sha256 over every line of data/probes/novel_ops/S_test_4way.jsonl EXCEPT the header, checked against the value pinned in readout_1_instrument before any scoring happens. IN THE ROW IDENTITY and load-bearing there: an accuracy is readable only against the floor and MDE registered for the items it was taken on, and this item set has been rebuilt through four versions. One ckpt under two hashes is two measurements, not a replacement. The FILE hash is deliberately not used -- the header carries the recorded battery maximum and moves whenever a rule is added, which happened once with the items byte-identical.

n.why: items scored, 1000 for the pinned set. Required because the registered MDE (0.4497/0.3755) was computed at n=1000 and a smaller denominator changes what it is compared against. The writer refuses rather than excludes an unscorable item, so this is 1000 or the run raised.

summed.why: THE REGISTERED READOUT: {program: accuracy} under summed-NLL option scoring, one entry per program, never a pooled number. Pooling is excluded by the prereg -- it read 0.2560 on v3 while one partition sat at z=+12.81 and the other at z=-12.19.

mean.why: {program: accuracy} under mean-per-token scoring, the NORMALISATION CONTROL and not a second readout. Taken from the same forward pass as `summed` (the score matrix is captured before argmax), because a control taken under a different numeric regime than the number it controls is not a control. A sign disagreement between the two on one program is evidence of a zero effect, which is how it read on 3 of 8 arm-program cells.

floor.why: the registered PRIOR LOWER BOUND per program (0.364 diamond_chain, 0.294 diamond_chain4), stored with every row so an accuracy is never read without it. NOT a chance floor and NOT a certificate: it is the maximum over the 29 heuristic rules in the builder's battery, i.e. what a rule-following adversary scores, and the leak family is unbounded. The prereg's OPERATIONAL floor is the control arm's own score on this file, which is why the readout is a difference.

mde.why: the registered minimum detectable ACCURACY per program (0.4497/0.3755), two-proportion, two-sided alpha=0.05, power=0.80, n=500 per program, null variance at p1 for both arms. Stored per row so the number a reader compares against travels with the measurement. As a required LIFT over the prior lower bound that is 8.57pt and 8.15pt.
